log_tail_full: +Impact: A paid-status refresh running alongside fulfillment work can silently move a lot out of Kelsey's newly created shipment. The panel can then show the wrong box contents, directly breaking the binding constraint that shipments are Kelsey-owned and re-import never reassigns an assigned lot.

+Fix: Omit `shipment_id` from the buyer-field update. Assign the default in a separate atomic update constrained with `.is("shipment_id", null)` (or in a transaction/RPC using `COALESCE` under a row lock), so a concurrent non-NULL assignment always wins.
+Finding: Failure to cancel sibling listings is invisible to the import, so a clean run can leave sold goods active on another channel.

+Evidence: `autoCancelSiblingListings` treats a failed sibling select as “no siblings” and only logs an update error (`app/src/app/actions/listing-actions.ts:48-75`). `updateListingStatus` ignores the helper's result and returns success (`app/src/app/actions/listing-actions.ts:666-684`), which `commitEoaImportChunk` records as a successful row (`app/src/app/actions/eoa-import-actions.ts:394-405`). The final stale-status check cannot detect this: `deriveSalesStatus` prioritizes any Sold listing over remaining Active listings (`app/src/lib/schemas/item-schema.ts:93-105`).

+Impact: An imported lot can be Sold on LiveAuctioneers while its eBay/Etsy sibling remains Active, yet the UI reports a zero-failure import and may close the auction. That creates a direct double-sale risk and defeats the shared artery side effect on which this batch relies.

+Fix: Make sibling select/update failures part of the `updateListingStatus` result and fail the EOA row. As a final guard, verify that imported item IDs have no other Active/Pending listings before permitting auction close.
+Finding: Commission and rep-payout lookup failures are silently converted into successful sales with missing or incorrect payout data.

+Evidence: The estate commission lookup does not inspect its error (`app/src/app/actions/listing-actions.ts:577-588`); when it fails, the main listing update still proceeds without recomputed commission/payout fields. Rep-user and tenant-default lookups also ignore errors and can write zero or the hard-coded 10% fallback (`app/src/app/actions/listing-actions.ts:623-647`). The listing update then returns success at `app/src/app/actions/listing-actions.ts:652-684`, and the EOA action marks the row successful at `app/src/app/actions/eoa-import-actions.ts:394-405`.

+Impact: The 74-row production run spans multiple estates, so a transient lookup failure can leave stale/null client and SB-SOS payouts—or an incorrect rep payout—while all CSV money columns and the dialog appear successful. Spot-checking one listing does not detect silent failures on the other rows.

+Fix: Treat job, rep-user, and tenant-default query errors as row failures before writing the Sold update. Recompute and write all commission/payout fields deterministically (including explicit clears when no commission applies), and prevent close when any lookup or payout calculation could not complete.

Re-running the same CSV cannot fix that item if it isn'"'"'t in the file (or isn'"'"'t ticked), so the operator is told to retry a fix that cannot work, with no way to distinguish it from a real per-row failure in the run they just did. In this specific production run the auction has no pre-existing Sold listings so it won'"'"'t misfire this time, but the mechanism itself isn'"'"'t scoped to what it claims to report on.

**Fix:** Track the item ids actually written Sold-successfully during this run (accumulate across chunks, e.g. via the row results) and check staleness only against that set, not `auction_id`-wide.

**Priority:** P2

**Confidence:** medium

**Finding:** Nothing in preview or commit prevents two different EOA rows in the same run from resolving to the same item; the second one silently overwrites the first'"'"'s committed sale with no error surfaced.

**Evidence:** `app/src/app/actions/eoa-import-actions.ts:366-444` — the per-row commit loop does an independent `updateListingStatus(listing.id, "Sold", …)` per row keyed only by that row'"'"'s own `itemId`; there is no set tracking `itemId`s already processed in this run (across chunks or within one). If row A resolves (or is manually picked in `needs_pick`, `eoa-import-dialog.tsx:2392-2413`, which offers every `pickableItem` with no filter excluding items already targeted by another ticked row) to the same item as row B, row B'"'"'s Sold transition finds the listing already Sold (via the `.in("status", ["Active","Sold"])` lookup at line 375-384) and treats it as an ordinary Sold→Sold refresh, overwriting row A'"'"'s `price_sold`/buyer/`buyer_premium` with row B'"'"'s values. Both rows report `ok: true`.

**Impact:** A single misclick in the `needs_pick` picker (or, generally, any two rows that end up pointing at the same item) causes one lot'"'"'s actual sale/buyer/money to vanish without any error, warning, or way to detect it after the fact from the commit summary — both rows look successful. **Fix:** Track `itemId`s consumed within `allSelectedRowIndexes` (or across the whole commit) and reject/flag a second row targeting an item another ticked row already claims, before writing.

**Priority:** P2

**Confidence:** medium

+Impact: A duplicate submission or two open import dialogs can abort a chunk before any of its listings are processed, after prior chunks or earlier buyer updates have already committed. The UI has no specified recovery for an action-level error without `results`.

+Fix: On 23505, reselect the buyer and continue, or use an atomic conflict-safe insert/reselect database function. Define the dialog's behavior for top-level chunk errors: stop immediately, do not close, and retain the exact unprocessed rows for retry.
+Finding: Buyer paid status is aggregated per 10-row chunk, not per buyer/import.

+Evidence: Task 4 defines `la_paid_status` as Paid only when every row in the buyer group is Paid (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-eoa-import-buyer-fulfillment.md:710-729`), but Task 5 calls `buildBuyerUpserts(chunkRows)` on only the current chunk (`:917-920`).
